submission.justification:
Module-D1 at 30% wall coverage gives the highest light collection of the eligible designs (39.4 PE/MeV), which is the stated goal. Module-D2 is eliminated because its 20-cycle failure rate is 30%, far above the 5% hard limit. Module-D1 and Module-D3 both have point-estimate failure rates under 5% (D1: 2%, D3: 0.5%), but both have a 95% upper bound of 13.2%, so neither is statistically shown to meet the hard limit with the current batch of 40. This is the main risk of this recommendation: D1's point estimate passes, but the sample is too small to confirm it. D1 is chosen over D3 because the failure-rate evidence does not clearly separate them (both share the same upper bound), and D1 gives 59% more light (39.4 vs 24.8 PE/MeV at 30%). Coverage is set at the 30% maximum because light yield rises monotonically with coverage. Before cryostat filling, I recommend a larger thermal-cycling test of D1 to confirm the failure fraction is at or below 5% at 95% confidence; if that test fails, the fallback is Module-D3 at 30% (24.8 PE/MeV, 0.5% observed failures).</justification>
